{{Short description|American chemist and inventor}}
{{use mdy dates|date=November 2025}}
'''Zalman Mordecai Shapiro''' (May 12, 1920 – July 16, 2016) was an American [[chemist]] and inventor. He received 15 [[patent]]s, including a 2009 patent on a process to make commercial production of [[diamond]]s cheaper,<ref name=patent>{{Cite web|title=Inventor, 89, has his eye on diamonds |url=http://www.marketplace.org/topics/tech/inventor-89-has-his-eye-diamonds |publisher=[[Marketplace]] |date=2009-06-16 |access-date=2009-06-16}}</ref> and played a key role in the development of the reactor that powered the world's first [[nuclear power]]ed [[submarine]], the ''[[USS Nautilus (SSN-571)|Nautilus]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Atom Contract Is Called Faulty |author=Unna, Warren Unna |publisher=[[The Washington Post and Times-Herald]] |date=1957-02-21 |page=A11}}</ref><ref name=numec1>{{Cite news |title=NUMEC made significant advancements |author=Thomas, Mary Ann |author2=Santanam, Ramesh |publisher=[[Valley News Dispatch]] |date=2002-08-28 |access-date=2009-06-17 |url=http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/valleynewsdispatch/s_88361.html }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Biography==
Shapiro was born in [[Canton, Ohio]], on May 12, 1920<ref name="who">{{Cite book|title=Who's Who in America - 2008 |edition=62 |year=2007}}</ref> to Abraham and Minnie ([[Married and maiden names|née]] Pinck) Shapiro.<ref name=who/> He graduated from [[Passaic High School]] in [[New Jersey]] as the [[valedictorian]] in 1938.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Patent Success |publisher=Johns Hopkins Magazine |date=2009-08-27 |access-date=2009-09-01 |author=Brown, Geoff |url=https://magazine.jhu.edu/2009/08/patent-success/}}</ref> He attended [[Johns Hopkins University]], earning [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]], [[Master of Arts|M.A.]], and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degrees in 1942, 1945, and 1948, respectively.<ref name=who/>

==Career==
After completing his education, Shapiro moved to [[Pittsburgh]], [[Pennsylvania]], and began a career in [[engineer]]ing and chemistry. He worked for [[Westinghouse Electric (1886)|Westinghouse Electric]] and the [[Bettis Atomic Power Laboratory]], where he worked on developing the fuel for the first commercial nuclear power plant, the [[Shippingport Atomic Power Station]].<ref name=numec1/> He founded Nuclear Materials and Equipment Corp. (NUMEC) in [[Apollo, Pennsylvania]] in 1957 to develop improved methods of processing nuclear fuel.<ref name=who/><ref name=numec1/> He was then investigated as part of the [[Apollo affair]].

In 2009, at age 89, Shapiro filed a patent for a new process of synthesizing diamonds. His family nominated him for the [[National Medal of Technology and Innovation]], where he received "dozens of recommendation letters", but was not recognized. Pennsylvania Senator [[Arlen Specter]] lobbied the [[Nuclear Regulatory Commission]] (NRC) on Shapiro's behalf. The NRC responded to the senator by letter in November of that year, stating that the organization was unable to "unequivocally conclude that nuclear material was not diverted from [NUMEC] nor that all previously unaccounted for material was accounted for during the decommissioning of the site."<ref>{{cite web |last=Johnson |first=Scott |title=What Lies Beneath |url=https://foreignpolicy.com/2015/03/23/what-lies-beneath-numec-apollo-zalman-shapiro/ |publisher=Foreign Policy |date=23 March 2015}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Shapiro married Evelyn Greenberg in 1945, and they have three children: Joshua, Ezra, and Deborah.<ref name=who/> He was formerly the president of the Pittsburgh chapter of the [[Zionist Organization of America]].<ref name=zoa1>{{Cite news|title=ZOA brings Catholic schools to Holocaust Museum |date=2001-04-12 |publisher=[[Jewish Chronicle]] |page=1}}</ref> Shapiro and his wife were honored in 2008 for their contributions to the Jewish community for over 60 years.<ref>{{Cite news|title=ZOA honors Del Duca, Shapiros for their lifetime achievements |date=2008-10-23 |publisher=[[Jewish Chronicle]] |page=4}}</ref> He lived in the [[Oakland (Pittsburgh)|Oakland]] section of Pittsburgh,<ref>{{Cite news|title=89-year-old Oakland inventor receives 15th patent |date=2009-06-26 |access-date=2009-07-05 |author=Jin, Liyun |publisher=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/09177/979949-28.stm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090629070606/http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/09177/979949-28.stm|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 29, 2009}}</ref> where he died at the age of 96.<ref name=obit1>{{cite news |url=http://triblive.com/obituaries/newsstories/10809808-74/shapiro-nuclear-fuel?printerfriendly=true |title=Scientist developed nuclear fuel for USS Nautilus |date=2016-07-18 |access-date=2016-07-19 |author=Thomas, Mary Ann |work=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809161622/http://triblive.com/obituaries/newsstories/10809808-74/shapiro-nuclear-fuel?printerfriendly=true |archive-date=2016-08-09 }}</ref>
